sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS CARE OF THE ELDERLY.  FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER FEELS ABOUT SENDING AN ELDERLY FAMILY MEMBER TO A NURSING HOME.  WHAT SHOULD ONE KNOW ABOUT THE NURSING HOME ENVIRONMENT WHEN MAKING THIS DECISION?
turns: Yeah, so I'm a manager at the grocery store, and honestly, I feel kinda weird talking about this since I haven't lost my parents yet, but I guess I've just made up my mind years ago that if the time comes, I'm not sending my folks to a nursing home.

Oh wow, that's bold, I guess? I mean, my dad went into a facility a few years back and honestly, I'm still kinda skeptical about it, mostly because... well, it wasn't the kind of care I thought we'd get.
I mean, looking back now, I realize I probably just wanted to keep my mom safe in a way that felt real, even if the reality wasn't always what I signed up for.

Yeah, exactly. It's just that my dad ended up in one when he was like 72, and honestly, I was terrified to call my mom because I saw how helpless everyone looked, like they were just... ghosts in those rooms.
I guess I didn't want them to just be numbers or someone else's responsibility anymore than they already were.
It's not the staff being bad, but the whole place felt so sterile, like everyone was just waiting for something that never happened.
I guess I just wanted to be there to see if she needed help, you know? Not just have someone check the meds while I was gone for work.

Yeah, it's just that I ended up being the one who had to go back in every Tuesday, and seeing her in a gown waiting by the door while I was at work... that's when I realized it wasn't about the facility at all.
That's really heavy to hear, but yeah, I get it—it's like the whole point of being family gets lost when you can't even see them walking down the hall without a gown.

Yeah, plus you're just waiting for the staff to tell you why they left you alone, and they won't tell you because they don't want trouble, so you end up wondering if anyone is actually paying attention.
I guess that's why I just can't bring myself to do it, even though the staff probably do their jobs fine.
Yeah, I guess I'm just afraid that if I do it, I'll never know if they're actually comfortable or just being ignored.
I mean, I guess the scary part is figuring out how to explain that to my own parents if they start asking why I won't put them there.
I mean, if my dad was still sharp enough to fight the system, I'd have stayed home, but once he stopped recognizing me, the only person who could argue for him was the one making the calls.
Yeah, but then they start asking me stuff I can't answer and I just want to tell them to go back to bed, but I feel like I'm the one letting them down.
And honestly, I don't think my parents deserve that silence anymore than I deserve to be the only one who knows the truth.
I mean, I think I'm just scared that if I let you handle it, I won't have the right to say I tried everything myself.
Yeah, but I guess for me it was already too late to say no once I saw where things ended up.
Yeah, but I guess I'd rather be the one getting yelled at than watching them disappear behind a door I can't open.
Yeah, I guess that's exactly where I landed, too—feeling like the only one who knew the truth but knowing it wasn't enough to fix it.
Yeah, it's just that knowing they're there feels like a kind of abandonment even if someone's actually watching them.
Yeah, maybe it's just the feeling that we're abandoning them to a place where they can't make mistakes anymore.
I guess that's just it, isn't it? Like we're keeping them in a bubble where they can't mess anything up, but that means they're not really living, you know?
Yeah, it's just that once you take them out of the chaos of the house, they stop making mistakes, but they also stop being there at all.
Yeah, it's like we're just preserving them in amber, but they're not really alive inside that amber anymore.
Yeah, I guess that's the whole point—once they stop messing up, they stop being there at all.
I guess it's just that protecting them from the world feels like killing the person they used to be.
I mean, maybe it's better to let them make mistakes while they can, before the silence takes over.
Yeah, I guess I'm the one who has to live with the guilt of choosing them over the world.
Yeah, but I'm the one who has to answer to my mom while she's gone to the house, and that's the silence that really eats you alive.
Yeah, but I guess I can't just sit with that silence knowing I didn't try to keep them here.
I guess I just have to learn to sit with the silence even if it hurts more than the argument ever did.
Yeah, I guess I'll just take the heat myself rather than watch them fade into that quiet.
Yeah, but I guess for me it's already done and done, so at least the silence isn't waiting anymore.
Yeah, maybe I just won't say anything if you ever ask, but I'd rather you know the real me than some quiet version of it.
Yeah, so maybe we both just had to pick our battles before the silence got too loud.
Yeah, maybe that's the only way to make sure they were actually seen before the silence wins.
Yeah, well, guess I'm just glad the silence isn't waiting anymore for me.
Yeah, I guess I just need to stop worrying that my choice is the only one that matters.
Yeah, well, guess I'll leave you with that thought.
